newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc seen up; copper, nickel to hold steady.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc seen up; copper, nickel to hold steady.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices are tipped to head higher later on Friday but may soon be hit by a mild correction, Far East metal traders said.
Nickel prices will be underpinned by the ongoing strike at Inco Ltd.'s Sudbury mine and smelter in Canada while copper is seen trying to punch its way back above US$2,500 a tonne, the dealers said.
"Zinc looks like it should go higher," a trader said.
"I feel it's oversold," a dealer for a European metal trading company said. "It's due for a correction, but it'll be quite mild. Fundamentally, zinc is still looking very good."
Another dealer predicted that zinc will run into brisk selling "as it approaches $1,400" a tonne.
Three-month zinc was quoted by the trade at 0200 GMT at $1,375/79 a tonne, a touch firmer from the close on the LME on Thursday of $1,375.
Nickel prices are seen getting support as the week-long Inco strike drags on, dealers said.
"People will begin to wonder how long the strike will go on. It should be well supported," a trader said.
The union representing Inco's 4,670 workers said on Wednesday it could take months for the dispute to be resolved. The mine was supposed to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel this year.
Asian dealers quoted three-month nickel at 0200 GMT at around $7,250/80 a tonne, up from the close on the LME of $7,240.
LME copper is expected to make an attempt at gaining a toehold above the $2,500 a tonne level later on Friday.
"I still feel it will try $2,500 this afternoon. It seems to have stabilised and built a foundation around $2,480," a European dealer said.
Another trader said copper should also benefit from the coattails of zinc's recent rise and placed resistance at $2,520.
"I think copper will eventually weaken, but not today," one dealer said. "There doesn't seem to be any reason for it to go down. When it does, it may go down very quickly."
Three-month copper was quoted by the trade at $2,488/93 a tonne at 0200 GMT against the close on the LME of $2,481 a tonne.
